scope: Proposition 8.5 (Macroscopic extremal-length bounds) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 62-63. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In every diverging-scale extraction, including the finite sphere, the following hold in the reference coordinate. 62 1. For every d > 0, the family of all discrete-surface paths whose projected diameter is at least d has a positive limiting lower extremal-length bound. 2. There is a deterministic c∗ > 0 such that every fixed round annulus A(z, r, 2r) in an ordinary coordinate chart has lim inf n ELXn (︁ H−1 n Ctr(A(z, r, 2r)) )︁ ≥ c∗. The assertion holds simultaneously for a countable dense annulus library, with strict margins. It includes annuli surrounding an isolated exceptional mark whose closures avoid the marks.
